content.text:
I found one claim the record doesn't support. Every other factual claim checks out against the record.

- **Flagged: contributing factor 1, "within the minute it was switched."** The document says legacy-checkout-fallback went off "for all account page traffic within the minute it was switched." It didn't. The flag was switched at 03:37:13 (P1). In that minute's evaluations it read off 152 times and still on 48 times (G7ad6). It read off for all 200 evaluations only from 03:38 (G7037). The first sentence of that factor ("No staged rollout or automatic guard was seen") is fine, because the record holds no such guard.
- **Root cause and causal-chain step 5:** I accepted these. They state Code-Fix's reading of the source and name F1 as their source. The root cause also says outright that it is unverified.
- **Causal-chain step 3:** I accepted the claim that the new renderer's path reaches the failing spend-summary code. It rests on C2 (a candidate cause) and on that revert being confirmed (T29), with the renderer switch shown in the logs (Gc27d).

I didn't judge the action items or the "had it been otherwise" what-ifs.

flags.quote: legacy-checkout-fallback went from on to off for all account page traffic within the minute it was switched.
flags.why: In the minute it was switched (03:37), 48 of 200 evaluations still read on; it read off for all evaluations only from 03:38.

supported.quote: With legacy-checkout-fallback off, account pages took a path where `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py` divides the month's total by the number of purchases this month. That list is empty for any shopper who has bought nothing this month, so the division raised ZeroDivisionError at line 47, and `serve_account_page` turned each one into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

An administrator switched off an older fallback for showing shoppers their account pages, which sent those pages through newer code that most likely breaks when it works out a shopper's average spend for the month if they have bought nothing that month.
If anyone switches legacy-checkout-fallback off again, account pages could fail again for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load

It did not change what was done: the investigation weighed it as unverified and reverted monthly-spend-feature first, and reverted legacy-checkout-fallback, the flag the lead named, only after the first action was refuted; that revert was confirmed, so the lead proved right.
Shoppers' account page requests failed: the error rate on account pages went up and stayed up.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.

Account pages were no longer served by the legacy renderer. The new renderer served them instead, and that path reaches the failing spend-summary code. This followed legacy-checkout-fallback reading off in the flag evaluations.
An admin switched feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off.
Feature flag monthly-spend-feature, which the same admin switched on at the same instant: turning it back off left the service at the incident's level, so it was put back.
On that path, the spend summary divides the month's total by the number of purchases this month, and that list is empty for any shopper who has bought nothing this month.
No staged rollout or automatic guard was seen on the flag change.

No check was seen that exercised the code path a flag switch turns on before the switch was made in production. Here that path was the new renderer's spend summary for a shopper with no purchases this month.
Two flags on the same service were switched by the same admin at the same instant, so the logs could not separate their effects.
Nobody was paged when the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop fired: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one

supported.quote: Every action taken was a flag revert that could be put back.

The response acted first on monthly-spend-feature, the higher-ranked candidate, even though the person's lead named legacy-checkout-fallback. That revert did not help, and account pages kept failing until the second flag was reverted.
